w: Built around 1855 as a summer villa for Empress Eugenie, it was sold in 1880 and became a hotel casino drawing Europe's elite, including regular guest King Edward VII. Fire gutted it in 1903; rebuilt within the original walls, it closed briefly in the 1950s and now runs as a Hyatt hotel on the beachfront.
s: Empress Eugenie's seaside villa turned royal hotel
_facts: Built c.1855 as a summer villa for Empress Eugenie
Sold 1880, converted into a hotel casino
Fire destroyed it in 1903; rebuilt within the original walls
Regular guest was King Edward VII; now a Hyatt hotel

n: Cité de l'Océan et du Surf
w: Opened in 2011, this Steven Holl-designed museum merges two ideas: 'under the sky' and 'under the sea'. Its curling roof shapes the public plaza and tilts toward the horizon, fronting 3,800 square metres of gallery space, an auditorium and a restaurant. It won the 2011 Emirates Glass LEAF Award.
s: Steven Holl's wave-roofed museum of ocean and surf
_facts: Opened June 2011, designed by Steven Holl Architects with Solange Fabiao
Concept built around 'under the sky' and 'under the sea'
3,800 sq m of gallery space, auditorium, restaurant
Won the 2011 Emirates Glass LEAF Award and 2012 American Architecture Award

w: Opened in 1933 in an art deco building on the Biarritz seafront, this aquarium is best known by its French name, Musee de la Mer. A 1992 renovation added a major new marine animal collection, and a 2009-2011 extension doubled the visitor area and added tanks, at the expense of its former bird space.
s: Art deco aquarium built into the Biarritz seafront
_facts: 1992 renovation added a major marine animal collection
2009-2011 extension doubled the visiting area and added tanks
Expansion traded away some of its former bird-keeping space
